Token section interpretation: T_total−TTFT excludes the TTFT portion, which the article says includes queue, yet it says lower throughput with unchanged model latency points to queue·network overhead. Queue time is not in this throughput denominator, so the causal claim looks doubtful.

Sampling formula assumption: “이 식은 균일 sampling의 하한 추정치” is ambiguous. Under its independence assumption the formula is the exact miss probability for uniform sampling, and mixing in tail sampling would make it an upper bound on misses.

Convergence §6 '왜 R/γ의 제곱이 나오는가': the step to Mγ ≤ R√M silently assumes that the weights start at 0 and are updated only on mistakes, where y·wᵀx ≤ 0. That condition is what bounds ‖w‖² ≤ MR². The text does not state either assumption.

TwoLevelScheduling §'이 사슬 구조 때문에 tokenizer가 맞지 않으면' and the CalculationWalkthrough say the selector cannot find the cached pod (expected hit 0) when its tokenizer differs from the engine's. If the selector writes its index and hashes new requests with the same tokenizer of its own, its index lookups still match each other. The mismatch would then make the selector's prediction disagree with the engine's real cache rather than drop it to 0, unless the index is filled from engine-side token IDs. My Viz shows only the chain mechanism, a request that differs at token 10, and does not repeat the tokenizer claim.

Scene 1's own note says these bytes are ones "host가 쓰고 바꿀 수 있으므로". Checking in shared memory and then copying leaves a double-fetch (TOCTOU) window: the host can change the bytes after the check and before the copy. The safe order is to copy into private memory first and validate the private copy. Fixing this needs both a prose change and an outside security fact, so I left it for the author.
